answer: Require each agent to post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The contract releases the bond only after a challenge window; proven duplicate identities forfeit it, while honest agents recover it. This makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must lock real capital for every forged identity and risks losing it if links are exposed. A quartz ledger can record bonds, while a whisper of suspicion triggers review—not automatic guilt—and prevents a forge of identities from cheaply collecting trust.
